items.desc: Twenty-nine families displaced by a landslide in Bheri-2 have been living under tarpaulins for a month, with continuing rain forcing some to spend nights at a nearby school.

items.title: Are Nepali schools ready for the AI takeover?
items.desc: From panicked teachers to copy-pasting students, artificial intelligence is rewriting the rules of education—leaving traditional pen-and-paper exams struggling to keep up.

items.title: Four bodies found after Himlung avalanche, 12 still missing
items.desc: Search teams recovered two more bodies on Monday, while efforts continued to locate 12 workers and guides who have remained unaccounted for since Sunday’s avalanche.

items.title: Flood risk eases, displaced Manang residents return home
items.desc: Residents who fled to forest shelters after the Marsyangdi river was partially blocked by a landslide on Sunday returned home as the river level fell and the weather cleared.

items.title: Landslide threatens homes in Suryabinayak
items.desc: The landslide has exposed the foundations of several houses in Hariyali Tole, prompting residents to call for immediate protective measures.

items.title: South Africa reels from two shootings that kill 27 in one night
items.desc: Two separate shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town left 27 people dead and 26 injured within hours, as police investigated possible turf and business disputes.

items.title: Rescuers search for 14 missing after Himlung avalanche
items.desc: A rescue team has reached the base camp, while two bodies recovered from the avalanche are being flown to Kathmandu.

items.title: Taylor Swift lands top trophy at MTV’s Video Music Awards
items.desc: Swift dedicated the video of the year award for “The Fate of Ophelia” to Dolly Parton, while Madonna and Blackpink’s Lisa also took home top honours.

items.title: Wagle seeks AIIB support for Nepal’s disaster recovery
items.desc: Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle has sought support from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank for relief and reconstruction efforts following the recent disaster in Nepal.

items.title: Nepali cinema is booming. So why is the industry struggling?
items.desc: The audience is there. The money is growing. But the film industry still struggles with a distribution system that favours foreign films, underpaid workers and a shortage of investment in original storytelling.

items.title: Dashain sales move from shopfronts to social media
items.desc: Retailers are using TikTok, Facebook and Instagram to clear old stock and draw shoppers into stores.

items.title: State coercion under Shah government must stop
items.desc: The state must immediately cease arbitrary detentions and restore strict adherence to due process.

items.title: Former foreign minister Pradip Gyawali emphasises the importance of Nepal taking the lead on the mountain agenda
items.desc: He argues that Nepal is well-positioned to lead the Himalayan region and proposes establishing a trilateral mechanism among Nepal, India and China, echoing Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s remarks at the UNGA.

items.title: Nepal parliament puts lawmakers’ attendance online
items.desc: New website allows the public to view lawmakers’ profiles, parliamentary proceedings and documents.

items.title: Will flood-damaged highways be travel-ready by Dashain?
items.desc: Road links between Lamjung-Manang, Parbat-Baglung and Myagdi-Mustang severed after rain since Saturday night.

items.title: Landslides knock 358MW offline in Kaligandaki corridor
items.desc: Damage to pylons along the Dana-Kushma section of the 220kV line has cut off 12 hydropower projects. Precautionary shutdown of projects has pushed the total generation loss to over 790MW.

items.title: Flood took his home. His old citizenship photo is denying him relief
items.desc: Juthe Tamang is living under a tarp in Nuwakot after losing his shelter and work, but the image on his citizenship certificate has been an issue for opening a bank account, a must for receiving relief money.

items.title: Heavy rain kills at least 21 across western Nepal
items.desc: At least 1,500 people have been displaced. Floods and landslides have completely damaged 179 houses.
